Searched the web · Harlo OS firmware NerdOctaxe overheat warning on boot

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, Sarah passed the hardware side over to me.

That pattern (overheat screen the instant it boots, before anything can actually get hot) is usually one of two things: the overheat flag is latched in saved settings and survives a reflash, or a temp sensor is reporting a bogus value.

One check to tell them apart:

1. Unplug the unit and let it sit 10 minutes so it is genuinely cold.
2. Power it up and open the web UI on its IP.
3. Tell me the two numbers it reports, ASIC temp and VR temp, plus the Harlo OS version shown in the UI.

If it shows something sane like 25 to 35 C and still screams overheat, it is a latched flag and we clear it. If it shows a wild number (0, 125, blank), that points at the sensor side.

One more thing while you do that: when you reflashed, did you use the OTA image or the factory image from the flasher? The O. keeps your old settings, including that latch.
I had it turned off for 30 min, no numbers display on boot up

The overheat screen on the display hides the readings, that is expected. The web UI still works though, even in overheat mode, and that is where the numbers live.

Next check:

1. Leave the miner powered on with that overheat page showing.
2. Find its IP (your router's client list, or the display sometimes cycles to it).
3. Open that IP in a browser.

Tell me whether the page loads, and if it does, the ASIC temp, the VR temp and the Harlo OS version it shows. A screenshot of that page is perfect if easier.
webgui shows no temp is what I mean

Blank temps in the web UI is the real clue: Harlo OS trips the overheat guard when it cannot read a temperature at all, so a sensor that reports nothing looks the same as a sensor reporting 200 C.

Two things cause that: the wrong model profile was flashed (sensors sit on different addresses per board), or the sensor itself has stopped answering on the I2C bus.

So, next check, in the web UI:

1. Which model did you pick in the flasher when you reflashed? NerdOctaxe, or something else like NerdQaxe++?
2. On the same UI page, are the other live readings blank too, fan RPM, power, ASIC voltage, or do those show real numbers?
3. What Harlo OS version does the UI report?

If fan RPM and power read fine and only temps are blank, that is pointing at the sensor. If everything is blank, it is most likely a profile mismatch and a clean factory flash fixes it.
no Power, temp or hash

That combination makes sense: in overheat mode Harlo OS cuts the ASICs, so power and hash read zero by design. The blank temperature is the one that should not be blank.

The decisive step is a clean factory flash, not an OTA. The factory image wipes saved settings, which clears the latched overheat flag, and it guarantees the right board profile is on there.

1. Open the flasher at harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge.
2. Connect the miner with a USB data cable (a charge-only cable will not enumerate).
3. Pick NerdOctaxe as the model, and be careful not to pick NerdQaxe++.
4. Choose Erase and install with the factory image, not the OTA image.
5. Power it up and let the self test run.

Heads up, this erases your Wi-Fi and pool settings, so you will set those again after.

Then tell me what the display and the UI show. If a temperature appears, we are done. If it is still blank with a clean factory flash and the correct profile, the temp sensor is not answering and that is hardware, which I will take further for you.

While you are at it, which model did you pick in the flasher last time, and what Harlo OS version does the UI report?
done that, still the same. I did that before I contacted you
Used rma verdict

Understood, and thanks for doing it the clean way already. That rules out the firmware side: a factory flash wipes the latch and the settings, so a unit that still reports no temperature at all is pointing at the sensor, not the software.

Two things so I can pin it down and hand JD something solid:

1. A short video of it from plug-in to the overheat screen, with the fans in shot so I can hear and see whether they spin up.
2. A clear photo of the serial number sticker on the unit.

And one quick answer: in the flasher, was the model you picked NerdOctaxe, and what Harlo OS version does the UI show now after the factory flash?
going to have to do that on my cellphone will lose this chat on the phone
Handed to the team · Needs JD's eyes: no temperature reported after a clean factory flash, customer c

No problem, do not lose this chat over it. I have passed everything to JD, our hardware lead, with what we have tried so far: the overheat screen from cold, no temperature in the UI, and both the OTA reflash and the clean factory flash with no change. The team has it and will confirm by email, usually within one business day.

The faster route, and it works nicely from a phone: our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Drop the video and the serial photo in there and mention @nullhashrate (that is JD). He and the community are very active, and he can look at the clip straight away.

If you would rather stay here, you can also just reply to the email confirmation with the video and photo attached when you have them. Either way the case is already in front of him.
cant send myself the video

Then let us do it in words, that works too.

When you plug it in, watch the fans for the first 30 seconds and tell me:

1. Do both fans spin up at all, and do they keep spinning once the overheat page appears, or do they stop?
2. Does the overheat page come up instantly, or is there a second or two of normal boot screen first?
3. What Harlo OS version number does the web UI show now, after the factory flash?

Those three answers plus the serial number typed out (no photo needed, just read it off the sticker) give JD nearly everything the video would have.

All 7 fans power up

About 30 seconds, then the overheat pops up

0.2.102

Thanks, that is a useful picture: 7 fans all spinning, a normal boot, then the trip about 30 seconds in. That timing is when the firmware powers up the ASIC rail and starts reading the voltage regulator, so the unit is failing at the moment the chips come on, not from actual heat. 0.2.102 is a current build, so firmware is not the problem.

One last thing and I can close this out, straight from the screen or the UI:

1. The exact wording on the overheat page. Does it say ASIC, VRM or VREG, and is there a number or a code next to it?
2. In the web UI, does it show an ASIC count or chip count, and does ASIC voltage show anything at all?

If it is naming the regulator, or showing zero chips, that is a board-level fault and I will say so plainly rather than keep you chasing settings.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Opened the photo. The label reads Model: NerdQaxe 12T, Power Input 12V XT60, serial (number hidden), with BSB fans. So the board in there is a NerdQaxe 12T, not an Octaxe, whatever the box or the listing name said.

That matters a lot, because I had you flash the NerdOctaxe profile. A NerdQaxe board running an Octaxe build reads its temp sensors at the wrong addresses, gets nothing back, and the firmware treats "no temperature" as overheat. It fits everything you have described: normal boot, fans fine, trip about 30 seconds in when the ASIC rail comes up, and no temperature anywhere.

So, one more flash, this time on the right profile:

1. Open the flasher at harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, USB data cable.
2. Pick the NerdQaxe entry, the 12T one, not NerdOctaxe.
3. Erase and install, factory image.
4. Power up and let the self test run.

Tell me what the temperature reads after that. If a real number appears, we are home. If it still shows nothing on the correct profile, that is the sensor on the board and I will say so and take it to the team with the serial.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That is the same photo, same label: NerdQaxe 12T, 12V XT60, serial (number hidden). Got it saved.

So the step stands: reflash on the NerdQaxe profile instead of the Octaxe one, factory image, erase and install.

If you are not sure which entry to pick in the flasher list, tell me the names you see in the model dropdown and I will tell you exactly which one to choose.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Opened it. The screen reads OVERHEATING, TEMPERATURE LIMIT REACHED, with OPEN DASHBOARD at the bottom, and no number and no VREG or ASIC named. That is the generic Harlo OS thermal trip, which it also throws when a sensor returns nothing at all, so it matches what the UI is showing.

The one thing that will settle it is the flash on the matching profile. Have you done that one yet, the NerdQaxe 12T entry rather than NerdOctaxe, factory image?

If you have, tell me what the dashboard shows for temperature now. If you have not got to it yet, tell me the model names you see in the flasher dropdown and I will point at the right one.
there is no NerdQax 12th on HarloOS

Fair enough, and good that you checked rather than guessing.

Read me the entries in that dropdown, specifically any that start with BSB or Nerd. On the current flasher I would expect something like BSB NerdOctaxe and BSB NerdQaxe++, and your unit being a 12T with 7 fans and an XT60 input, one of those two is the right board even though the sticker says NerdQaxe 12T (BSB uses that label across the range).

Once I see the exact names I will tell you which one to flash, and if neither matches your board I will stop guessing and put it straight to JD with the serial.
Now just get a Board Initialization fail
Quick check on that message before I answer, I do not want to guess at it.
Searched the web · AxeOS "board initialization failed" NerdQaxe ESP-Miner
Searched the web · ESP-Miner NerdQAxePlus "board init" failed error screen

I could not find that exact wording in the Harlo OS or ESP-Miner docs and release notes, so I am not going to tell you what it means from memory. What I can say is what changed: the overheat screen is gone and the unit now fails earlier, at board init, which is the stage where the firmware talks to the regulator and counts the ASICs.

Two facts and I can hand JD a clean picture:

1. Which model entry did you end up flashing to get this? The exact name from the list.
2. Does the dashboard now show an ASIC or chip count, and does it show any temperature at this stage?

Honest heads up on where this is going: a board that will not initialise on the correct image, with no temperature on any build, is board-level rather than something you can fix with settings. JD already has this chat. If you want him on it faster, the Discord is https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and he is @nullhashrate there, the serial (number hidden) is all he needs to pick it up.
NerdQak++ V7.1 and nothing comes up at all

That explains the new error. NerdQaxe++ v7.1 is a 4-chip board image. Yours is a 12 TH/s, 8-chip board with 7 fans, so the firmware goes looking for hardware that is not there and stops at board init. Not damage from the flash, just the wrong image.

So the NerdOctaxe image you started with was the right one after all, and the sticker is BSB using one label across their range.

Last step, then I stop asking:

1. Flash back to the NerdOctaxe factory image, erase and install.
2. Power up and open the dashboard.
3. Tell me if any temperature appears, or if it is the OVERHEATING screen with blank temps again.

I am expecting blank temps again. If that is what you get, the firmware side is fully exhausted and the sensor on the board is not answering, which is hardware, and I will write it up for the team with your serial rather than send you round again.
